title: Arithmetic Rigidity of Analytic Functions and Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers
summary: Let $\mathscr L$ denote the set of Liouville numbers. We prove a local arithmetic rigidity theorem for real-analytic functions. If $U\subset\mathbb R$ is an open interval and $f:U\to\mathbb R$ is real-analytic with $f(\mathscr L\cap U)\subseteq\mathscr L$, then $f$ is the restriction to $U$ of a rational function in $\mathbb R(x)$. Quantitatively, there exists an absolute constant $τ>2$ such that, for every nonrational real-analytic function $f$ and every nonempty open subinterval $V\subset U$, the set of $ξ\in V\cap\mathscr L$ satisfying $μ(f(ξ))\leqτ$ contains a Cantor set.
